tasksTab.title: Tasks table
tasksTab.intro: You are on the Tasks tab now. This short lesson shows how to look through recordings before you annotate them. Afterwards it sends you back to Annotate.

steps.title: Tasks table
steps.hint: Every recording of the project is one row here, with its status badges.

steps.title: Move with ↑ ↓
steps.hint: `↓` and `↑` move the highlighted row. The list scrolls with it.

steps.title: Open a preview
steps.hint: Click an empty part of a row (not the recording name, which is a link) to open its spectrogram preview. Click it again to close it.
steps.task: Click an empty part of a row

steps.title: Pin previews
steps.hint: Press `p` to pin the open preview. Pinned previews stay open while you move on, up to 5 at once, so you can compare recordings.

steps.title: All shortcuts
steps.hint: Click {icon:help} or press `?` to see every shortcut of this table, then close the list with `Esc`. Tip: `Shift` + click ticks several rows for bulk actions.
steps.task: Open the shortcut list with `?`, then close it

steps.title: Back to Annotate
steps.hint: The lessons continue on the “Annotate” tab at the top of the page. Click it.

steps.title: Welcome to Sonari
steps.hint: This tour teaches you to annotate recordings, in about 30 minutes and at your own pace. You need no prior experience with Sonari. Each recording is one lesson. This card shows the current step and ticks it off when you have done it; collapse it with the arrow at the top any time.

steps.title: The spectrogram
steps.hint: The picture of the sound: time runs from left to right, frequency from bottom to top, and brighter means louder. Each box on it is a sound event: one call someone marked and tagged with its species. A box spans the call's duration and its frequency range. Annotating means checking these events, correcting them and adding missing ones.

steps.title: The action bar
steps.hint: All tools for the spectrogram live here, for example hide {icon:hide-spectrogram}, zoom {icon:zoom}, the sound event tools {icon:create} {icon:select} {icon:delete}, settings {icon:settings} and the player. Hover a button to see its shortcut. The next lessons use them one at a time.

steps.title: The Tasks table
steps.hint: Click “Tasks” at the top of the page. A short lesson of 6 steps runs there. When it is done, click “Annotate” to come back and continue here.

steps.title: Status badges
steps.hint: When you are done with a recording, give it a status badge. It saves your verdict and opens the next recording. In this tour, the next recording is also the next lesson. Any badge works here: click one or press `1`–`4`.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Listen
lessons.intro: Bat calls are ultrasonic. Played slowed down, they help you find calls and hear their rhythm. The species itself you identify from the call shape in the spectrogram.

steps.title: Play
steps.hint: Press `Space` or click {icon:play} to play and pause. Bat calls are ultrasonic, so Sonari plays them slowed down to make them audible.

steps.title: Speed
steps.hint: Change the speed in the {icon:speed} menu. Slower stretches the calls further and lowers their pitch.

steps.title: Repeat & autoplay
steps.hint: {icon:loop} repeats the visible part. {icon:autoplay} starts playback on every recording you open. A filled, ringed button is switched on.

steps.title: Seek
steps.hint: Double-click the spectrogram where playback should start. A red line shows the current position.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Moving around
lessons.intro: Recordings are often longer than the screen. Moving quickly through them lets you check every call.

steps.title: Drag to pan
steps.hint: Click and drag the spectrogram sideways. Trackpad scroll gestures work too.

steps.title: Overview strip
steps.hint: This strip shows the whole recording. The green window marks the part you see above. Drag the window, or click anywhere in the strip to jump there.
steps.task: Click or drag in the overview strip

steps.title: Arrow keys
steps.hint: `←` and `→` move in time, `↑` and `↓` in frequency. With `Shift` held, `←` and `→` switch to the previous or next recording.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Zoom
lessons.intro: Short and faint calls are easy to miss, and their shape is what tells species apart. Zooming in shows both.

steps.title: Zoom mode
steps.hint: Press `z` or click {icon:zoom} to switch on box zoom.

steps.title: Box zoom
steps.hint: Drag a rectangle around one call. The view zooms to exactly that area: now you see where the call starts and ends in frequency and how steeply it falls.

steps.title: Step zoom
steps.hint: `+` and `-` zoom in and out in time. Hold the Control key as well (Ctrl, also on a Mac) to zoom in frequency.

steps.title: Reset
steps.hint: Press `u` or click {icon:reset} to see the whole recording again.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Sound events
lessons.intro: Sound events are the core of annotation: each one marks a call and carries its species.

steps.title: Create
steps.hint: Press `c` or click {icon:create} to switch on create mode. Then drag a box around one call, from its start to its end and from its lowest to its highest frequency. Take the bright call at about 0.9 s: it is boxed already, but drawing your own on top is fine for practice. Zoom in {icon:zoom} first if the call looks tiny. The new event is selected right away.

steps.title: Details
steps.hint: This panel shows the selected event: a zoomed preview, its tags and its measurements. Events created by an AI model also show how confident the model was.

steps.title: Deselect
steps.hint: `Esc` clears the selection.

steps.title: Select
steps.hint: Press `s` or click {icon:select}, then click an event. Drag its corners to make it fit the call.

steps.title: Jump between events
steps.hint: `n` jumps to the next event, `b` back to the previous one. No scrolling through long recordings.

steps.title: Delete
steps.hint: The event at about 4.9 s, high up at 150 kHz, is tagged “this: is wrong”: it is not a call. Select it (`n` jumps there) and press `x`, or switch on delete mode {icon:delete} and click it.

steps.title: Undo
steps.hint: Deleted the wrong one? `Ctrl+z` brings it back. Undo works for events and tags. Try it now.

steps.title: Redo
steps.hint: `Ctrl+Shift+z` or `Ctrl+y` redoes it, so the mislabeled event is gone again.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Tags
lessons.intro: Tags say what a sound event is. A wrong or missing species is the error you will fix most often.

steps.title: Remove a wrong tag
steps.hint: The event at about 1.6 s is tagged “this: is wrong” next to its species. Select it, then click that tag to remove it, or press `d` for a picker. Careful: `x` and delete mode {icon:delete} remove the whole event, `Ctrl+z` brings it back.

steps.title: Add the right species
steps.hint: This recording is from a Bechstein's bat. Add “species: Myotis bechsteinii” to the same event: press `a` or click “Add tags” and start typing “bechsteinii”.

steps.title: All events at once
steps.hint: Tag actions work on the selected event. With no event selected (`Esc` deselects), they work on every event of the recording: `r` replaces a tag everywhere, `Shift+a` tags all untagged events. To change only one event, select it first: jump to it with `n`, or press `s` (or click {icon:select}) and then click it.

steps.title: Task tags
steps.hint: Task tags describe the whole recording instead of one call, e.g. when a file holds only noise or insects. Add any task tag here.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: View settings
lessons.intro: Every recorder and every species looks different. Adjusting the view makes faint calls stand out.

steps.title: Spectrogram settings
steps.hint: Press `o` or click {icon:settings}. Try another colormap or frequency range and watch the spectrogram change. “Save” keeps the settings for every recording and closes the panel; `o` or `Esc` closes it without saving.
steps.task: Open the settings, then close them

steps.title: Hide spectrogram
steps.hint: `h` or {icon:hide-spectrogram} hides spectrogram and waveform, e.g. to look at the events alone. Press it again to bring them back.

steps.title: Hide sound events
steps.hint: `Shift+h` or {icon:hide-events} hides the events, so you see the plain spectrogram. Show them again afterwards: only visible events can be selected and edited.

steps.title: Full page view
steps.hint: `w` or {icon:fullscreen} shows only the spectrogram, scaled to your screen. `w` again closes it.
steps.task: Open and close the full page view

steps.title: Shortcuts
steps.hint: Click {icon:help} or press `?` for every shortcut on this page. `Esc` closes the list.
steps.task: Open the shortcut list, then close it

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.intro: Time to put it together on your own.

steps.title: Filters
steps.hint: Filters narrow down the recordings you work through, e.g. by date, time, station, tag or status badge. Press `f` or click {icon:filter} “Filters” and look through the list, then close it with `Esc`. During the tour, filters are not applied, so the lessons stay in order.

steps.title: Finish the remaining tasks
steps.hint: Listen, check every event, fix wrong tags and add missing calls. Then give the recording a status badge.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

steps.title: Notes
steps.hint: Every recording has notes for questions, remarks or problems, visible to your team. Mark a note as an issue (shown in red) to flag a problem. Delete your own notes with the trash icon.

steps.title: Your feedback
steps.hint: How was the tour? Unclear steps, missing features, bugs, ideas: all welcome. Press `q` to jump into the note field, write your note and save it with `Shift+Enter`. `Esc` leaves the field.

steps.title: Tour complete
steps.hint: Well done! Click “Finish tour” to go back to the home page. You can continue or restart the tour there any time.

lessons.title: Sound events
lessons.intro: Sound events are the core of annotation: each one marks a call and carries its species.

steps.title: Time intervals
steps.hint: Bird calls are marked as time intervals: a start and an end time across all frequencies, not boxes. Press `e` to open the shape menu next to {icon:create}, then choose {icon:interval} “Time interval”.

steps.title: Create
steps.hint: Press `c` or click {icon:create} to switch on create mode. Then click where a call starts, hold the mouse button and drag to where it ends. Overlapping an existing event is fine here. The new event is selected right away.

steps.title: Details
steps.hint: This panel shows the selected event: a zoomed preview, its tags and its measurements. Events created by an AI model also show how confident the model was.

steps.title: Deselect
steps.hint: `Esc` clears the selection.

steps.title: Select
steps.hint: Press `s` or click {icon:select}, then click an event.

steps.title: Resize
steps.hint: Drag the start or end edge of the selected event so it fits the call exactly.

lessons.title: Replace tags
lessons.intro: Sometimes a whole tag is wrong, not just missing. Replace swaps it in one step instead of removing and adding.

steps.title: Listen first
steps.hint: One event is tagged Graureiher (grey heron). Play the recording with `Space` and listen whether you can hear a heron.

steps.title: Replace a tag
steps.hint: Select the Graureiher event, then press `r` and replace its tag with “this: is wrong”.

steps.title: All events at once
steps.hint: Add, delete and replace work on the selected event. With no event selected (`Esc` deselects), they work on every event of the recording. To change only one event, select it first: jump to it with `n`, or press `s` (or click {icon:select}) and then click it. `Ctrl+z` undoes any of them.
